info.name: searxng-integration-test
info.description:
Direct requests to the local SearXNG instance (container/docker-compose.yml), the same way a metasearch client (Firecrawl, Hermes, a browser bookmark) calls it. SearXNG has no authentication: whatever address SEARXNG_HOST publishes (container/.env) is an open search proxy for that network.

container/core-config/settings.yml must keep search.formats [html, json] - without json, clients get 200 responses with no results array.

The last request covers liferay_forum, a fork-local engine. The other two external sources probed for this fork - learn-answer and bankier.pl - render client-side and return nothing useful over plain HTTP, so they are Firecrawl scrapes and live in the firecrawl project's collection, folder "External sources (Firecrawl scrape)". Firecrawl's own view of this instance (/v2/search mappers) is there too.

{{searxngUrl}} is a collection variable so these run without an environment; point it at the published host. Nothing here needs the firecrawl stack to be up.

The collection carries one pre-request guard: a request whose host variable does not resolve to a real URL is skipped with a console warning naming the variable, which is what a shared-link copy (no collection variable, no environment selected) produces.

request.description: safesearch=2 is strict, and it is the only thing /v2/search safe:true adds to the SearXNG request (search/v2/searxng.ts sends it only when safe is set, otherwise the instance default applies). How much each engine honours it varies, so this asserts the parameter is accepted and the query still answers rather than pinning a result count. The Jev filter that runs on top of safe:true is a separate stage, covered by the Search Safe Filter folder.

item.description: searx/engines/liferay_forum.py, a fork-local engine over the Discourse search.json endpoint at discuss.liferay.com. It needs no browser, which is why it is an engine and not a Firecrawl scrape, unlike the other two sources in this repo. The endpoint ANDs the search terms, so a phrase with no hits returns no results key at all rather than an error. Discourse rate-limits anonymous clients hard: a burst gets a 180 s suspension, reported in unresponsive_engines.

item.name: SII: single GPW company (orlen)
item.description:
searx/engines/sii.py, a fork-local engine over the server-rendered search page at
sii.org.pl/szukaj. The parameter is `search`, NOT `q`: /szukaj?q= returns HTTP 200 and one
identical 62,576-byte page for EVERY query including a nonsense one, so the wrong parameter
reads as a healthy engine that found nothing. The site also serves an empty 5.4 kB shell to a
bare 'Mozilla/5.0' or 'curl/8.5.0' but a full page to any realistic agent string, so the engine
identifies as SearXNG/1.0 rather than leaning on curl_cffi's browser impersonation.
A query matching nothing answers 404, not an empty 200, which is why the engine sets
raise_for_httperror = False. Every query here returned 10 results on 2026-10-11.

Note the two outcomes this request accepts. Measured 2026-10-11: sii.org.pl serves two
searches from a burst and answers 429 after that, and newman sends requests back to back with
no pacing, so a throttle is expected on a full-collection run. The assertion requires that a
throttle is NAMED (unresponsive_engines carries 'too many requests'); an empty result with no
reason attached still fails, because that is indistinguishable from a genuinely empty search.

exec: pm.test('The engine answered, or said why it did not', () => {
// sii.org.pl rate-limits hard (measured: 2 searches, then 429) and this
// collection fires four back to back with no pacing, so a throttle is a
// legitimate outcome. What is NOT acceptable is an empty result with no
// reason attached - that is indistinguishable from 'nothing matches'.
const throttled = bad.some(u => JSON.stringify(u).indexOf('too many requests') !== -1);
if (throttled) { console.log('   (throttled by sii.org.pl - accepted)'); return; }
pm.test('Every result is a sii.org.pl ARTICLE url', () => {
// /<id>/<section>/<slug>.html. A wrong query parameter (?q=) still returns HTTP
// 200 and a plausible page, which is why this asserts the host AND the shape:
// an author (/autor/) or advert (click.php) link would not pass.
pm.test('Results carry a title and a summary', () => {
pm.test('Summaries are prose, not the date line', () => {
// One markup variant writes the date/author line as class="above metas"; a
// parser matching only class="notes" returns the date as the summary.
pm.expect(dated, 'the date leaked into the summary: ' + JSON.stringify(dated.map(r=>r.url))).to.have.lengthOf(0);

item.name: DNA: US-listed card (alibaba)
item.description:
searx/engines/dnarynkow.py, a fork-local engine over dnarynkow.pl/spolki/?search=.
Two things mislead here. The search is a PARAMETER on the stock index, not a search page:
there is no /szukaj route, no WordPress REST API and no sitemap entry, so every path-shaped
probe 404s while ?search= works. And the result rows are server-rendered into the HTML body,
not into the ~2.5 kB __NUXT_DATA__ payload, so decoding the payload concludes 'client rendered,
nothing here'. robots.txt names ClaudeBot, Claude-User, Claude-SearchBot and a dozen other AI
agents under `Allow: /`; only /pulpit is disallowed and is never requested.

item.description: searx/engines/ksiazak.py, a fork-local engine over the PUBLIC WordPress REST API rather than scraped HTML. The archive is six posts about six companies, measured 2026-10-11 - and that is the product, not a shortfall. A rare hit means a dedicated analyst picked that company, which is why this source earns a place despite returning nothing for most queries. Noctiluca SA is a 0.14% holding here; the other five posts cover Atrem, Dino Polska, Scanway, Kolejkowo and Grupa Kęty.

item.description: WordPress `search` matches the title AND the body, so 'orlen' returns the Atrem note because ORLEN is discussed inside it. Recorded because the instinct is to treat that as a false positive; it is the source working correctly, and a coverage check must not silently discard it. Orlen is the second-largest GPW weight in the DeGiro book and has no post of its own.
